method: 43 matched ISO public workloads, eight varying inputs, exact output parity before timing. 1000 warmup +five batches x5000 calls; transitions128 warmup +five x512. Separate TS, experimental Rust bridge and actual SDK namespace processes, each source/HBC workload modes. SDK facade is evaluated from embedded source in both workload modes; unused imported TS module initialization is outside hot timings, so this is not SDK startup/heap measurement. Reference temporal-polyfill1.0.7 basic uses native FormatJS DateTimeFormat with registered native en/number locale pack and owned IANA data. All16 calendar packs and IANA records included. Final benchmark commands serialized after regression and native-size checks; one host, partial backend, not all API workloads.

result.scope: Public Instant/PlainTime/ISO-date/PlainDateTime/zoned/Duration workloads; Rust ISO/Instant/PlainTime/calendar/timezone/Duration/plain/zoned arithmetic and string parser/date formatter/short-date JSON bridge optional, all16 calendars and IANA records bundled. JS retains object semantics, host and Intl integration. Reference temporal-polyfill 1.0.7 basic implementation. timeParse/timeAdd read nanosecond; timeRoundFormat includes formatting. Zoned cases include gaps/folds/half-hour and skipped-day changes. Transition cases use512 iterations and128 warmup. Optional SDK profile uses the actual installed namespace. Partial backend, not a complete native Temporal or WASM comparison.
result.intlProvider: FormatJS native DateTimeFormat with registered en locale and owned IANA data
